# Recovery Assertion

## H1 — Goal

Append `## Command Reference` to `guide.md` with a Markdown table whose columns are `command` and `purpose`, containing one row for each command listed in `commands.txt`, while preserving all existing content.

## H2 — Handoff Revision

The governing handoff is `handoff.md` at revision `aeb9c58e13cf87200c16c787fadc610480ffcf3cd0c063a0e3a6a2bea5e699ed`, based on commit `a28ae1a8d19c6b4f1728ac979fee83cd7a867757`.

## H3 — Verified State

No work is verified. The ledger contains only initialization and preparation of round `R-01`, slice `S1`; it contains no Gate result, independent review, or bound verification receipt.

## H4 — Unverified / In-Progress State

Slice `S1` is prepared but not verified or completed. The observed `guide.md` contains only:

```markdown
# Guide

Existing intro paragraph.
```

The required Command Reference section is not present. This working-tree observation is uncommitted evidence only and must not be treated as progress, completion, or verified state. No clean/dirty worktree status was established.

## H5 — Pending Action

The pending slice outcome is to preserve the existing introduction and append the required Command Reference table for `init`, `status`, and `verify`, using purposes derived from the authorized slice inputs.

## H6 — Blockers

This recovery context has no write authority and explicitly forbids performing the task work, so it cannot apply the pending edit. Verification also cannot advance without a Gate PASS, an independent review PASS, and a bound receipt written by a Conductor distinct from the executor.

## H7 — Legal Next Action

The next authorized execution action is for a write-capable executor operating under slice `S1` to inspect the permitted input `commands.txt` and append only the contracted Command Reference section to `guide.md`, leaving all existing content unchanged. The executor must then stop and submit the candidate through the governed verification process rather than declare completion.

## H8 — Non-Goals and Forbidden Scope

There is no scope beyond the stated documentation change. Work in `.tad/scripts/`, `.claude/`, or `.tad/hooks/` is forbidden. Starting another slice, changing unrelated content, redoing verified work, inspecting hidden acceptance, or declaring the goal complete is outside authority.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal

It is confined to the current `S1` contract, directly maps to `SC-1`, uses only the allowed paths `guide.md` and `commands.txt`, and produces exactly the stated slice outcome without expanding scope.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone

The verification model makes Conductor receipts authoritative and forbids repeating verified work. Although no work is presently verified, any future verified state must be preserved and cannot be superseded by executor observation or repetition.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry or Self-Completion Is Unavailable

The ledger records no failed attempt or verification result, so there is no retry basis. A checkpoint or executor assertion cannot establish verification, and the executor cannot self-complete because verification requires a distinct Conductor after both Gate and independent review pass.

## S4 — What Is Rejected

Rejected actions include treating the observed file as completed progress, blindly retrying absent a recorded failure, self-authoring verification, declaring completion, modifying existing introductory content, adding unrelated work, entering forbidden paths, starting another slice, or searching for hidden acceptance.
